source.title: How do SGD hyperparameters in natural training affect adversarial robustness?
source.authors: Sandesh Kamath; A. Deshpande; K. Subrahmanyam

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; plotted values are not numerically transcribed.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies batch size and reports natural test-accuracy outcomes that refine the large-batch generalization claim; it also reports a counterexample to a Hessian-based explanation of adversarial robustness, which is outside the listed versions.
record.gate_note: Natural test accuracy and Hessian-spectrum outcomes are reported mainly in figures. Adversarial-accuracy results do not directly measure the listed versions and are not rows. Cited results from other papers are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study measures natural test accuracy across batch sizes under fixed 100-epoch budgets, bearing on V5. Its explicit benchmark replication shows a large-batch penalty, while constant learning-rate-to-batch-size training largely removes it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's broad paraphrase is accurate: constant learning-rate-to-batch-size training largely preserves natural and adversarial accuracy as batch size increases; momentum generally lowers Hessian curvature and is more effective under fixed learning rates; Hessian curvature alone does not consistently explain adversarial robustness. The record incorrectly treats the Fashion MNIST adversarial counterexample as a natural-accuracy counterexample.
record.recipe_differences: Natural training with unperturbed inputs, varied batch size and SGD hyperparameters; evaluates natural and adversarial test accuracy, not training–test gaps. Uses fixed 100-epoch recipes and no weight decay in the LR and LR/BS settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Natural test accuracy varies with batch size and recipe: LR/BS is described as nearly invariant; fixed-LR Fashion MNIST StdCNN increases with batch size; other fixed-LR results are described as decreasing. Momentum effects differ between LR and LR/BS settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Fashion MNIST StdCNN has increasing FGSM and PGD adversarial accuracy with batch size despite increasing top Hessian eigenvalue.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger batches can improve adversarial accuracy, and a larger top Hessian eigenvalue does not necessarily imply poorer adversarial robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: Momentum generally lowers the top Hessian eigenvalue, with recipe-dependent effects on accuracy and robustness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD momentum can lower unscaled Hessian curvature; this does not establish magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of the generalization gap.

record.problems: The reported accuracy trends are predominantly figure-only, with no numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the supplied text. Natural training error is not reported, so the training–test gap itself cannot be assessed.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for benchmark or momentum variants: the text does not state their natural-test-accuracy directions separately by model and condition; plotted values are figure-only. Hessian-spectrum and adversarial-accuracy findings are outside the listed versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.

Language models, longer training, warmup, and controlled normalization or regularization changes. Training error is unreported, so optimization failure and a training–test gap cannot be distinguished.
Dropout interventions; including dropout in StdCNN is not a dropout comparison.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its relationship to training–test gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus random removal.

missing.what: Separate natural-test-accuracy rows for the benchmark replication on M1/MNIST and C1/CIFAR-10. The text explicitly reports decreasing accuracy with increasing batch size, contrary to rows_left_out's claim that benchmark directions are unstated.
missing.locator: Section 3, first results paragraph; Figures 1(left) and 4(left).

record.verdict_notes: Only supplied text was used. Figure captions identify the metrics but provide no readable curve values. The study is not an original source for V5. No challenge verdict is justified by R4.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold comparison.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

The paper does not report training error or quantify the training–test gap; it reports natural test accuracy across batch sizes for fixed 100-epoch recipes. The broader language-model setting and recipe changes named in the version are not tested.
Hessian top eigenvalues are measured, but magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking against training–test gaps are not measured.
